subject: Service of process, emergency relief carveouts & escalation protocol -- MSA redlines
messages:
From: Sonia Ramirez <sonia.ramirez@federalpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@federalpay.com
Date: 2026-08-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines — service of process & injunctive relief

Jordan — thanks for sending the draft MSA. Our legal team flagged two items we need to resolve before commercial sign-off: service of process and your carveout for injunctive relief. High level:

- Service of process: FP prefers a consent-to-service clause (in addition to permitted methods) to avoid jurisdictional disputes in the US.
- Injunctive relief: we need clarity on whether injunctive relief is excluded from arbitration or if emergency relief may be sought in court only in very narrow circumstances (data protection/key escrow etc.).

I've attached our annotated MSA extract (MSA_ServiceOfProcess_annotated.txt) and a short note from our GC. Can we get Redwood's proposed language and an outline of the escalation steps (who to call if we need emergency relief)? Also, any objections to listing a single point of contact for service?

Thanks — Sonia
Sonia Ramirez
Head of Legal Operations | FederalPay
sonia.ramirez@federalpay.com

Sonia — thanks, received. Looping in our legal counsel (Laura) and Contracts (Kim) so we can respond with proposed language and an escalation contact list. Quick notes from my side:

- We generally accept a consent-to-service option but prefer not to concede exclusive jurisdiction for the life of the agreement.
- For injunctive relief, Redwood wants a limited carveout so we can pursue emergency relief to stop IP/data exfiltration — but we can narrow the carve to defined categories and a fast escalation path.

Laura / Kim — can you propose redlines (MSA + Order Form) and a compact escalation protocol (names/roles/expected response SLAs)? Sonia, I'll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min sync if that helps.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sonia Ramirez <sonia.ramirez@federalpay.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed redlines — service of process and emergency relief carveout

Sonia / Jordan — reviewed FP's annotations. I've drafted targeted redlines (see attached Redwood_MSA_redline_FP_20260827.docx) and summarized the rationale below. Please note these are intended for negotiation — happy to take direction from FP counsel.

Summary of proposed position:
- Service of process: add optional consent-to-service language but explicitly preserve Redwood's right to seek relief in any competent forum; no exclusive forum language. We propose a clause that permits service by certified mail, email to a legal address, and consent to service if FP elects — with a 30-day cure notice for technical defaults.
- Emergency relief: keep injunctive relief carveout for claims regarding confidentiality, IP, and data protection. Narrow the carveout to "limited equitable relief for preservation of confidentiality or prevention of imminent data loss" and require immediate escalation to Redwood's Legal & CS leads.
- Escalation protocol: two-tier contact list (operations escalation: 1hr response SLA, legal escalation: 4hr SLA during business hours), with after-hours escalation phone numbers.

Open points for FP counsel: whether to accept non-exclusive consent-to-service language and whether FP will accept the limited injunctive carve as drafted (we are not comfortable with blanket court access outside the carve).

Next steps: Sonia / FP counsel to confirm if Fenwick (or your outside counsel) wants to take call tomorrow at 11:00 PT. If yes, we'll send a calendar invite and share the redline in DocuSign-friendly format.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redline_FP_20260827.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: Fenwick LLP - Michael Cho <michael.cho@fenwick.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sonia Ramirez <sonia.ramirez@federalpay.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-28T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines — service of process and emergency relief carveout

Laura / Sonia — Michael Cho on behalf of FederalPay. Quick thoughts from FP's end after internal review:

- Consent to service is fine, but FP will push for at least a limited waiver of objections to venue for actions based on FP's use of the service (to reduce gamesmanship). FP is open to a non-exclusive clause that states both parties consent to service in the state of Delaware and accept personal jurisdiction there for claims not subject to arbitration.
- On injunctive relief, FP wants the ability to seek emergency injunctive relief for consumer funds-related issues and fraudulent transactions — FP is amenable to Redwood's "defined categories" approach but requests clarifying language that ties emergency relief narrowly to "imminent financial or consumer-harm events".
- We are comfortable taking a 30-min call; would prefer the afternoon (3pm PT).

If Redwood can provide (a) a redline that includes the consent-to-service optional text and (b) a one-page escalation protocol with names/phone numbers, we can take those to FP GC before the call.

Michael Cho
Fenwick LLP (counsel to FederalPay)
